title: A Fast Way to Become an Auto Mechanic: How Long Does It Really Take?
summary: How long does it take to become an auto mechanic? Explore this role and how to pursue a career in the industry with training from UTI!
body_markdown:
Automotive technicians solve problems, work with their hands and stay on the cutting edge of vehicle technology. From diagnosing issues to repairing advanced systems, they play a key role in keeping cars on the road.


If this sounds like your kind of work, keep reading. With training at Universal Technical Institute you can train to become an auto mechanic and start pursuing roles in the field in just one year!1,7 This guide will break down exactly what it takes.


## What Does It Take To Be a Mechanic?


Becoming a mechanic requires a blend of[automotive skill](https://www.uti.edu/programs/automotive/traits) , technical training, problem-solving abilities, physical stamina and attention to detail. It is essential to understand various mechanical systems, from engines and transmissions to electrical and hydraulic systems.


Mechanics must be adept at diagnosing issues using diagnostic tools and repairing or maintaining a wide range of vehicles and equipment. Physical stamina is crucial, as the job often involves lifting heavy parts and working in challenging conditions. Attention to detail ensures repairs are done correctly, preventing future issues and ensuring safety.


Continuous learning and certification can also help techs keep up with advancing automotive technologies and industry standards. Mechanics can specialize in areas like automotive, diesel, motorcycle or heavy equipment.


## How To Prepare for a Career as an Automotive Mechanic


According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), employers prefer that[automotive technicians have completed a postsecondary program](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/installation-maintenance-and-repair/automotive-service-technicians-and-mechanics.htm#tab-4) .


In many cases, formal training can help give an applicant an advantage over someone who has not completed any. That’s because automotive technician training shows an employer you already have the skills and knowledge you need to succeed in an entry-level position, which reduces time needed for on-the-job training.


If you know you want a[career as an automotive technician](https://www.uti.edu/programs/automotive/careers) , the good news is that programs start every few weeks at Universal Technical Institute (UTI), so you can dive in when you’re ready.1 As long as you meet the educational requirements, you can enter into a program with no previous experience required!


[Read: UTI Admissions Requirements](https://www.uti.edu/admissions/admissions-requirements)


## How Long Is Automotive Mechanic School?


Most automotive schools take one to two years to complete. The automotive technician program at[Universal Technical Institute](https://www.uti.edu/home) takes just 51 weeks to complete.[7](https://www.uti.edu/blog/education/automotive-technician-career#utiDisc)


The[program](https://www.uti.edu/blog/education/automotive-technician-training) includes[automotive courses](https://www.uti.edu/programs/automotive/courses) in subjects like engine service and repair, powertrains and transmissions and vehicle brake systems. You’ll even learn how to service electric vehicles! Each course is three weeks long and builds upon previously learned knowledge.


[Read: Auto Mechanic Courses at UTI](https://www.uti.edu/programs/automotive/courses)


## Automotive Mechanic Education Requirements


While high school automotive courses provide a good automotive technician background, high school graduates typically need formal automotive technician education to become fully qualified,[according to the BLS](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/installation-maintenance-and-repair/automotive-service-technicians-and-mechanics.htm) .


The BLS states that the best preparation for entry-level automotive technician positions is a trade school or postsecondary education program. These programs provide students with hands-on practice on vehicles.


Students can learn in a supportive environment where making mistakes is acceptable so they can eventually gain foundational automotive skills. This eliminates the need for extensive on-the-job training, although technicians at all stages in their careers continue to learn as new automotive technology emerges.


## What Are the Requirements To Attend Automotive Mechanic School?


Specific requirements to attend automotive technician school vary across institutions. At UTI, for example, the[requirements](https://www.uti.edu/admissions/admissions-requirements) include students being at least 18 years old, or 16 with a guardian’s signature.


They also must have achieved one of the following: graduated high school, received a GED certificate or equivalent.


Tuition varies from program to program, but at UTI, there are[automotive technician school grants and scholarships](https://www.uti.edu/financial-aid/scholarships-grants) available, as well as other[financial aid](https://www.uti.edu/financial-aid) options, to help students pay for school.10


[Read: Paying for Trade School: Financial Aid, Grants and Loans](https://www.uti.edu/blog/education/paying-for-trade-school-financial-aid-grants-loans)


## Automotive Mechanic Certification Programs Available


Upon graduating UTI’s core automotive program, graduates receive a diploma, certificate or associate degree, depending on the campus, that confirms their completion of the program. Those who choose to pursue[Manufacturer-Specific Advanced Training](https://www.uti.edu/programs/automotive/specialized-training) can get additional in-depth training featuring a variety of brands.


UTI graduates are also prepared to complete[Automotive Service Excellence (ASE) examinations](https://www.uti.edu/blog/automotive/mechanic-path-ase-certification) and may use their UTI training as one of the two years of experience required to become ASE certified. As the most-recognized standard for automotive technician excellence in the industry, ASE certification is highly valued by automotive dealerships and other employers.


[Read: Why ASE Certification Matters for Auto Tech Careers](https://www.uti.edu/blog/automotive/ase-certification-improve-your-auto-career-opportunities)


## Is Becoming an Automotive Mechanic the Right Career for You?


Automotive technicians do a lot of problem-solving work. They use computers to diagnose vehicle issues and physically examine cars. They use hand tools and power tools to make repairs and replace parts. In addition to physical labor, automotive technicians can expect the need to be excellent communicators and provide clear and friendly customer support.


If this skill set interests you, you may be a good fit for a career as an automotive technician. Plus, an interest in cars, technology and design is essential.


[Find Your Perfect Trade Program: Take Quiz](https://www.uti.edu/program-quiz)


## What Are the Job Prospects for Automotive Technicians?


According to the BLS, the[number of vehicles in use is expected to continue to rise](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/installation-maintenance-and-repair/automotive-service-technicians-and-mechanics.htm#tab-6) , which means more entry-level service technicians will be needed to work on these vehicles.


In 2024, the largest employers of automotive mechanics and service technicians were as follows:


Automobile dealers: 32%


Automotive mechanical and electrical repair and maintenance: 26%


Self-employed workers 14%


Automotive parts, accessories and tire stores: 6%


## Automotive Mechanic FAQs


### Is it hard to become a mechanic?


Becoming a mechanic takes commitment and hands-on learning, but it is achievable with the right training.18 Most challenges come from learning technical systems and keeping up with new vehicle technology.


### What is the fastest way to become a mechanic?


The fastest path is completing a focused automotive training program that combines classroom instruction with hands-on lab experience. This allows students to build job-ready skills in a shorter time than learning only on the job.


### Is it worth going to school to become an auto mechanic?


For many students, formal training is worth it because employers often prefer candidates who already have foundational skills. Training can also reduce the amount of time needed for on-the-job learning.


### Is it hard to get hired as a mechanic?


Entry-level opportunities are available across dealerships, repair shops and service centers. These roles may be easier to land with formal training, as employers value hands-on skills and technical knowledge.


Many trade schools, like UTI, also have relationships with employers looking for new talent. Some UTI grads even find jobs while they’re still in school!1
